extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners and USPTO examiners (applicants, attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on requirements, processing, and examiner treatment of Requests for Continued Examination (RCE) under 37 CFR 1.114, including what constitutes a proper submission, fee/payment rules, handling of improper or conditional RCEs, and special situations (after final, after allowance, after appeal, new matter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission content required by 37 CFR 1.114(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission may include an information disclosure statement (IDS), an amendment to the written description, claims, or drawings, new arguments, or new evidence in support of patentability. If a reply to an Office action is outstanding, the submission must meet the reply requirements of 37 CFR 1.111.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments previously filed (e.g., in an after-final reply) that were entered but not found persuasive may satisfy the submission requirement if they are responsive within the meaning of 37 CFR 1.111 to the outstanding Office action. A statement that incorporates by reference the arguments in a previously filed appeal brief or reply brief may be acceptable. See form paragraphs 7.42.04 and 7.42.08 for examiner use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of RCE fee under 37 CFR 1.17(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: An RCE must be accompanied by the proper fee(s) including the RCE fee under 37 CFR 1.17(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the RCE fee is missing the RCE is improper; applicant will be notified and the RCE will not toll running times for reply. Conditional authorizations to charge (see conditional RCE) are treated as payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application type and filing-date eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for continued examination under 37 CFR 1.114 the application must be a utility or plant application (not a design application) filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) on or after June 8, 1995, or an international application filed under 35 U.S.C. 363 on or after June 8, 1995 that complies with 35 U.S.C. 371. The RCE must be filed on or after May 29, 2000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CPA practice under 37 CFR 1.53(d) does not apply to utility and plant applications filed on or after June 8, 1995 (effective July 14, 2003). Special handling applies for design applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosecution must be closed when filing RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: Prosecution in the application must be closed (e.g., the last Office action is a final rejection, notice of allowance, or an Office action under Ex parte Quayle, or the application is under appeal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical support personnel verify prosecution is closed as part of initial processing. If prosecution is not closed, applicant will be notified, any amendment/reply will be entered, and the application forwarded to the examiner under 37 CFR 1.111.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE must be filed while application is pending
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must be pending (i.e., not patented or abandoned) when the RCE is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the time period set in the last Office action has expired, applicant may need to file a petition under 37 CFR 1.137 to revive an abandoned application (with required submission or fee).

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue fee / petition requirement when issue fee already paid
rubrics_metrics.description: If the RCE is filed after payment of the issue fee, a petition under 37 CFR 1.313 to withdraw the application from issue must be filed and granted for the RCE to be effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If issue fee already paid and no petition is filed/granted, payment of the RCE fee and submission will not avoid issuance of the patent. Applicant may not obtain a refund of the previously paid issue fee; if prosecution is reopened and subsequently allowed, the Notice of Allowance will reflect the difference in issue fee owed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliant inventor's oath/declaration for national stage applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application is a national stage application under 35 U.S.C. 371, a compliant inventor’s oath or declaration for each inventor must be submitted prior to or with the RCE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical support personnel verify this in initial processing (see subsection III(H)).

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE unavailable during court review
rubrics_metrics.description: An RCE will not be processed if the application is undergoing court review at the Federal Circuit or in federal district court because the application is in the jurisdiction of the court and the RCE procedure is not available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If discovered, the RCE will not be processed and the applicant will be notified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper RCE notification and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If one or more conditions for filing an RCE have not been satisfied, applicant will be notified (generally by mailing Form PTO-2051, 'Notice of Improper Request for Continued Examination (RCE)'). An improper RCE will not toll running of any time period set in the previous Office action for reply to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an examiner discovers an improper RCE forwarded in error, return the application immediately to an HSLIE. Examples include missing fee, missing submission, ineligible application type, or RCE filed after issue without a granted petition under 1.313.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambiguous transmittal papers (CPA vs RCE)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a transmittal paper is ambiguous as to whether it is a Continued Prosecution Application (CPA) under 37 CFR 1.53(d) or an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114, for plant or utility applications filed on or after June 8, 1995 the Office will treat the transmittal paper as an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114. For design applications, an ambiguous transmittal will be treated as a CPA under 37 CFR 1.53(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other papers filed with the transmittal paper will not determine whether the paper is a CPA or RCE. An unambiguous RCE filed in a design application will be treated as an improper RCE and Form PTO-2051 will be mailed. An RCE is not convertible to a new application; conversion of an improper CPA to an application under 37 CFR 1.53(b) is only done if extenuating circumstances exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional RCEs treated as paid when authorization to charge deposit account provided
rubrics_metrics.description: If a submission is accompanied by a 'conditional' RCE and payment authorization to charge the 37 CFR 1.17(e) fee to a deposit account (in the event the submission would not otherwise be entered), the Office will treat the conditional RCE and payment as if an RCE and payment of the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(e) had been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows processing of RCEs where entry of the accompanying submission is conditional on acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of amendments with a proper RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: If the conditions for filing an RCE have been satisfied, previously filed unentered amendments and amendments filed with the RCE will normally be entered. Amendments are entered in the order filed absent specific instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant wants certain previously filed after-final amendments not entered, provide specific instructions when filing the RCE. Applicants are encouraged to file all desired amendments no later than filing the RCE to avoid disapproval of entry under 37 CFR 1.111(b). If conflicting amendments exist, applicant should clarify which to enter. See MPEP § 714.03(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for claims when filing RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant does not need to pay a fee for excess claims previously paid for prior to filing the RCE. New claims in excess of the number previously paid for, filed with the RCE or thereafter, will require payment of the appropriate fees under 37 CFR 1.16.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure correct payment for any newly-added excess claims when filing RCE or subsequently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper CPA treated as RCE (post-July 14, 2003 rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant files a request for a CPA on or after July 14, 2003 of a utility or plant application filed on or after June 8, 1995, the Office will automatically treat the improper CPA as an RCE of the prior application under 37 CFR 1.114.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the CPA does not satisfy 1.114 requirements (e.g., lacks a submission under 1.114(c) or fee under 1.17(e)), it will be treated as an improper RCE and the prior time periods will continue to run. Use form paragraph 7.42.15 to notify applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: After final rejection: withdrawal of finality if RCE proper
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant timely files an RCE with the fee under 37 CFR 1.17(e) and a submission that meets the reply requirements of 37 CFR 1.111, the Office will withdraw the finality of any Office action to which a reply is outstanding and the submission will be entered and considered (see 37 CFR 1.114(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mere request for and payment of the fee will not toll running of time periods; the submission meeting reply requirements must be timely received to continue prosecution. Use form paragraph 7.42.04 to notify applicant that finality has been withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not fully responsive submissions: bona fide attempt requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reply to a final Office action is outstanding and the submission is not fully responsive to the final Office action, the submission must be a bona fide attempt to provide a complete reply to the final Office action in order for the RCE to toll the period for reply. If not a bona fide attempt, the RCE should be treated as improper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of non-bona fide submissions: an IDS alone when reply is outstanding; an amendment that cancels all claims and does not present any new or substitute claims. If not bona fide, prepare Form PTO-2051 and the application will not be tolled and may be abandoned after statutory period. If bona fide but not fully responsive, applicant is given a shortened statutory period of two months to complete the reply (see 37 CFR 1.135(c)) and Form paragraph 7.42.08 should be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-compliant amendment handled as bona fide attempt
rubrics_metrics.description: An RCE filed with an amendment that is not in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121 but that is a bona fide attempt to provide a complete reply should be treated as a proper RCE and a Notice of Noncompliant Amendment should be mailed. Applicant is given two months from mailing date to provide an amendment complying with 37 CFR 1.121.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 714.03 for amendment practice. Use Form paragraph 7.42.08 to set the shortened statutory period when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of claims for a different invention is not a basis for RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants cannot file an RCE to obtain continued examination on the basis of claims that are independent and distinct from, or lack unity of invention with, the claims previously elected and examined as a matter of right (i.e., applicant cannot switch inventions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an RCE is filed with an amendment canceling all claims drawn to the elected invention and presenting only claims drawn to a nonelected invention, the RCE should be treated as a proper RCE but the amendment should not be entered; applicant should be given two months to submit a complete reply. See 37 CFR 1.145 and MPEP § 821.03; use form paragraphs 8.04 or 8.26 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: New matter prohibited (35 U.S.C. 132(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment shall introduce new matter into the disclosure of the invention (35 U.S.C. 132(a)). Any amendment entered pursuant to 37 CFR 1.114 that is determined to contain new matter should be treated in the same manner as a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 determined to contain new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant seeks to add new matter to the disclosure, the RCE procedure is not available; the applicant must file a continuation-in-part (CIP) application under 37 CFR 1.53(b). See MPEP §§ 608.04-608.04(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: First Office action after RCE may be made final only in limited circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: The action immediately subsequent to the filing of an RCE with a submission and fee under 37 CFR 1.114 may be made final only if the conditions set forth in MPEP § 706.07(b) are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It would not be proper to make final a first Office action immediately after an RCE if the first Office action includes a new ground of rejection. Use form paragraph 7.42.09 when appropriate; the form paragraph explains that the action is final when claims are patentably indistinct or have unity with prior claims and could have been finally rejected on the record art.

rubrics_metrics.name: After allowance or Quayle action: reopening prosecution and issue fee implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing an RCE with the fee under 37 CFR 1.17(e) and a submission in an application that has been allowed will reopen prosecution if the issue fee has not been paid. If the issue fee has been paid, payment of the RCE fee and submission without a petition under 37 CFR 1.313 to withdraw the application from issue will not avoid issuance of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If RCE filed after issue fee paid, a petition under 37 CFR 1.313 must be filed and granted to reopen prosecution; applicant may not obtain a refund of the issue fee. Use form paragraph 7.42.05 to notify applicant that prosecution has been reopened when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: After appeal but before Board decision: RCE withdraws appeal and reopens prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant files an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114 after the filing of a Notice of Appeal to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board but prior to a decision on the appeal, it will be treated as a request to withdraw the appeal and to reopen prosecution before the examiner, regardless of whether the RCE is proper or improper. The Office will withdraw the appeal upon filing of an RCE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should advise the Board when an RCE is filed in an application containing an appeal awaiting decision; otherwise the Board may refuse to vacate a decision rendered after filing (but before Office recognition) of the RCE. If the RCE is proper (fee paid and submission responsive within meaning of 1.111), the Office will withdraw finality and enter the submission.
